title: On the Impact of Performative Risk Minimization for Binary Random Variables

repair_verification.details: Exact binomial threshold repairs and squared-mean risk expression analytically verified; local code-expression repairs checked without simulation reruns.

summary: Even-sample positive-tie estimator in the proof is evaluated by a negative-tie formula, yielding a wrong exact risk and reversed impact signs in an admissible case. Three bounded Minor concerns are retained separately.

problems.title: Binomial tie boundary evaluates a different estimator
problems.claim: For alpha>=1/2, proof defines theta=+1/2 if samplemean>=0 and-1/2 otherwise, then gives Etheta=1/2-F(m/2).
assumptions: Independent binary observations on{-1/2,1/2} withpositive probability3/4
All predicted and induced means stay in[-1/2,1/2]
problems.check: Enumerate K=0,1,2 withmasses1/16,6/16,9/16; positive-tie actions-1/2,+1/2,+1/2 and conditional losses3/16,1/16,1/16.
problems.counterevidence: Oddm tie absent; formulas are valid for negative-tie estimator, which matches released notebook formulas. Both endpoint tie choices are legitimate plug-in minimizers.
problems.impact: Exact finite-sample moments/risk/impact analysis is a core contribution, and the demonstrated sign reversals directly affect it under the estimator explicitly defined. Full-information and qualitative side-effect conclusions not refuted.

correction.positive_tie: Etheta=1/2-F(ceil(m/2)-1); addtie massq_m to printed moment, subtract2(1-alpha)p0q_m fromrisk, add(1-alpha)q_m tobias andalphaq_m toshift.
correction.negative_tie_alternative: Define positive branch only forsamplemean>0 andnegative for<=0; printed formulas then valid.
correction.verification: analytic event partition and exact enumeration
correction.limits: No plot regeneration or author adoption.

acceptance_check.truth_and_assumptions: The proof defines positive tie assignment, then uses an inclusive binomial CDF assigning the tie to the negative branch.
acceptance_check.decisive_evidence_and_counterevidence: At alpha=3/4, p0=pi=1/4 and m=2, the stated estimator gives Etheta=7/16, risk=9/128 and impacts (3/64,9/64), versus 1/16,15/128 and opposite signs from the printed moment. Odd m and the released negative-tie convention are valid counterevidence to a broader rejection.
acceptance_check.core_dependency_and_severity: Major: the invalid finite-sample moment derivation changes the paper's principal impact measures under its explicit estimator. Ease of tie-convention repair does not reduce this core dependency.
acceptance_check.correction_scope: Use F(ceil(m/2)-1) for positive ties or define negative ties consistently; no empirical rerun or author adoption is claimed.
